payload.title: Stream Sockets
payload.summary: Build bounded POSIX stream-socket loops with explicit framing, partial-I/O handling, and monotonic deadlines.

prerequisites: C17 arrays, pointers, explicit lengths, and fixed-width integers
File descriptors, byte order, and the POSIX socket lifecycle
outcomes: Explain why TCP is a byte stream rather than a message transport
Complete sends and exact receives despite partial system calls
Recover application boundaries with length-prefixed frames
Distinguish EOF, truncation, timeout, capacity, malformed input, and system errors

payload.exercise: Complete exercise.c with shared absolute-deadline helpers, partial-I/O loops, framed send/receive, and one-connection echo service behavior.
payload.reference: Use solution.c to compare behavior only after implementing the lesson.h contract.
checks: Back-to-back and fragmented frames over local streams
Oversized declarations that leave payload bytes unread
Clean EOF, truncation, and bounded timeout
Ephemeral 127.0.0.1 service behavior, descriptor cleanup, and listener flag restoration

allowed: Bounded monotonic deadlines on Linux and macOS
excluded: External networking, DNS, raw sockets, or packet capture
Privileged or fixed ports, INADDR_ANY, subprocesses, or shell commands
A general-purpose or internet-facing echo daemon
